signals.name: Micron
signals.label: Whale conviction fracturing even as Congress keeps buying
signals.detail: Soros added 7.9x (2,824 -> 22,422 sh, ~$25.9M) in Q2-2026, but Tepper cut his Micron stake 41% and Druckenmiller dumped it entirely the same quarter. Congress has been unusually active: 8 purchases vs 3 sales in the past 6 months (Reps. Newhouse, Rulli, Gottheimer, Sen. Whitehouse among buyers), some sitting on gains as high as +229% since Feb 2026 buys. Rep. Michael Rulli's newly-surfaced Aug 7 filing adds an NVDA sell to his book (see congress list) rather than fresh MU activity.
signals.takeaway: Chip-memory conviction is fracturing among whales (Soros in, Tepper/Druckenmiller out) even as Congress keeps buying -- a name to watch for a re-convergence next quarter rather than a clean consensus signal today.

signals.name: Nvidia
signals.label: Sharpest whale divergence of the Q2-2026 cycle, now heading into FQ2 earnings
signals.detail: Tepper added (+53,500 sh to 1,525,000, ~$305M); Dan Loeb (Third Point) exited 100% (sold all 190,000 sh); Soros bought NVDA puts (bearish overlay); Rep. Michael Rulli's Aug 7 late-filing batch disclosed a fresh NVDA sell alongside AAPL, adding a congressional data point on the bearish side. Burry's SOXX short (~9% NVDA-weighted, via Substack, no longer 13F-reportable) is reportedly working after SOXX fell ~21% in July. Monday 24 Aug: NVDA fell -2.3% alongside a broader chip selloff (Micron -5.8%, AMD -3.3%, TSM -3.7%) as AI-capex-fatigue positioning built into Wednesday's print, now one trading day away.
signals.takeaway: Three schools of smart money took three different sides on the same stock last quarter, and Wednesday's FQ2 print (after Monday's pre-earnings chip selloff) is now the immediate real-world test of which read was right.

signals.name: Alphabet
signals.label: Still the broadest whale magnet, and now the busiest congressional name too
signals.detail: Berkshire added 48,144,587 shares (+$21.1B, SEC EDGAR primary) and Loeb quadrupled his stake to 1,025,000 shares in Q2-2026 -- but Pershing Square (Ackman) fully exited Alphabet the same quarter to help fund a Microsoft/Meta add, and Tiger Global trimmed its Alphabet position while rotating into AI-chip names (Cerebras, AMD). A CNBC 'Warren Buffett Watch' piece (22 Aug) reports Buffett, not Abel, may still be the one calling the shots on major stock decisions post-retirement, citing a 'stealthy weekend call' behind the GOOGL add -- interpretive color on the same trade, not a new position. Congress: David Taylor (11 Aug) and Josh Gottheimer (Jul 24 trade / Aug 10 filing, refined date) both bought GOOGL.
signals.takeaway: Near-unanimous whale conviction has genuine cracks (Ackman full exit, Tiger Global trim); still the most broadly held AI mega-cap and now flagged as possibly still Buffett-directed rather than Abel's independent call.

signals.name: Silver
signals.label: Rally holds through the weekend into a live Monday sanctions catalyst
signals.detail: SLV +4.47% Wed 19 Aug, +2.75% Thu 20 Aug, +1.72% Fri 21 Aug to close at $62.72 -- three straight up sessions after the Treasury buyback surprise pulled real yields and the dollar down. GDX +9.42%/+2.59%/+2.98% and SILJ +9.55%/+0.67%/+0.95% across Wed-Thu-Fri; SLVP closed Fri at $40.85 (+1.44%). GC=F/SI=F futures remain low-trust this run (thin/rolled contracts) -- GLD ($423.36, +1.95% Fri) and SLV are the cleaner proxies. Insider selling clustered in silver/gold miners Aug 19-20 (Hecla's VP Sustainability fully liquidated 23,994 sh on 20 Aug; three Coeur Mining executives sold Aug 19) -- routine profit-taking into strength, not a reversal signal. Monday 24 Aug: SLV eased -0.83% to $62.20 (a pause, not a reversal) while GLD extended to a 3-month high (+0.79% to $426.69). Tuesday 25 Aug (price spine): SLV +0.19% to $62.32, GLD +0.32% to $428.07 (fresh high), GDX +1.91% to $105.52, SILJ +2.44% to $32.79, SLVP +2.31% to $41.67, NEM +2.50% to $135.14, GOLD(Barrick) +2.29% to $46.85, PAAS +1.08% to $54.21, AG +1.97% to $21.24, HL +2.55% to $20.92 -- a broad, miner-led resumption of the up-trend after Monday's pause.
signals.takeaway: The debasement trade resumed broadly across metals and miners Tuesday after Monday's one-session pause -- Wednesday's Nvidia earnings and Friday's Jackson Hole (Warsh's debut) remain the next two catalysts that could test or extend the move.

signals.name: Energy Fuels
signals.label: Bridgewater's new stake rode out Thursday's dip; Monday's China-sanctions rollout is a fresh wildcard
signals.detail: Bridgewater Associates took a new $2.3M/160,899-share position in Q2-2026 (SEC EDGAR), layering onto CEO/director open-market buys ($12.70-13.08, 7-8 Jul) already on record. UUUU fell -6.40% Thu 20 Aug in the broad AI-fear-driven rare-earth risk-off, then rebounded +8.92% Fri 21 Aug to close at $15.14 (MP Materials similarly: -2.89% Thu, +9.10% Fri to $60.05) -- both names round-tripped the sector-wide de-risking within two sessions. Treasury's Monday sanctions rollout explicitly threatens secondary sanctions on Iran's trading partners and named China (buyer of ~90% of Iran's oil) without confirming direct targeting -- a new China-trade-friction wrinkle that could sympathy-trade the rare-earth basket even though the direct catalyst is unrelated. Tuesday 25 Aug (price spine): UUUU jumped +7.33% to $15.97 and MP +4.79% to $60.17 -- both re-accelerating alongside the broader metals/miner move rather than fading the Monday pause.
signals.takeaway: A rare case of a macro whale and insiders both accumulating the same rare-earth name; Tuesday's fresh double-digit-adjacent moves in both UUUU and MP suggest the sector rally is broadening beyond precious metals into rare earths.
